description: Saves a new version of a knowledge entry with a new kind, title and body (send all three, the whole entry). Every earlier version stays in its history and can be brought back with restore_knowledge_version. Send the newest version number you read; if someone saved a newer version since, nothing is saved and the answer is stale with the newest number.

id.description: The part's or service's id (get_project_brief's topology lists them), or the area.

kind.description: component: one part of the project; resource: one service it uses; area: frontend, backend, data_storage, auth_access, infrastructure, integrations, observability, security, docs or tooling.

applies_to.description: What part of the project the entry is about, such as a house rule for the shop pages only. A part or service needs project_id; an area works for the workspace too. null: the whole project (or every project). Left out on update_knowledge, the entry keeps what it had.

body.description: The entry itself, in Markdown. Headings split it into the passages a search finds, so give each topic its own heading.

expected_version.description: The entry's newest version number when you read it (read_knowledge or list_knowledge_versions gives it). If someone saved a newer version since, nothing changes and the answer is stale with the newest number: read the entry again first.

kind.description: What the entry is, such as note, decision, house-rule, glossary, faq, brand-voice or style-guide (list_knowledge_kinds gives every kind and when to use it).

knowledge_id.description: The entry (list_knowledge and search_knowledge give ids).

project_id.description: The project the entry is in. May be left out: the entry's id finds its own project or the workspace.

title.description: A short title that says what the entry is about.

workspace_id.description: Workspace id from whoami; omit when there is one.

name: update_knowledge
title: Change a knowledge entry
